lines.j1: Java was created so one program could run on any machine: write once, run anywhere.
lines.j2: The compiler turns source code into bytecode, not machine code for one chip.
lines.j3: Each platform has its own Java Virtual Machine that runs the same bytecode.
lines.j4: The JIT compiler finds code that runs often, and turns those hot spots into fast machine code.
lines.j5: The garbage collector frees memory you no longer use, so you do not free it by hand.
lines.j6: Strong typing, a huge ecosystem and mature tooling make Java a safe choice for large systems.
